newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian dlr support survives choppy week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian dlr support survives choppy week.

text.p: The Australian dollar finished the session, and the week for that matter, on a steady note as range trading mentality exerted its all too common grip.

The steady finish actually belied a boisterous week in which support at US$0.7735 absorbed sustained selling only to have an offshore surge to six week highs at US$0.7822 evaporate under the glare of fresh offers.

The seesaw action confirmed dealer suspicions the currency had entered a period of consolidation after bouncing from a year low of US$0.7550 just a fortnight ago. Most felt there was still a modest bias to the upside but saw US$0.7820 as a ceiling.
By 5.00 pm (0600 GMT) the currency was back at US$0.7750/55 from US$0.7756/61 late Thursday and US$0.7740/45 last Friday.
It had reached as high as US$0.7822 offshore, its best levels since mid-January, after buying by U.K. and U.S. names sparked a vicious short squeeze past 78 cent resistance.

A sharp rally in gold prices was also cited as a supportive element -- the yellow metal is one of Australia's biggest commodity exports -- although dealers felt this was more a case of rounding up the usual suspects than a real influence.
But gains evaporated when sales emerged from sources as wide as Swiss banks, U.S. funds and Chicago IMM options players.

Japanese investors took up the bear cause and harried the dollar to 93.30/40 yen from 93.91/01 Thursday. Traders said this was just a small part of a worldwide phenomenon as investors, companies and banks realised profits on offshore holdings with the aim of padding balance sheets for the March 31 year-end.
The dollar found some support from an unexpectedly generous Bank of Japan which added excess liquidity to the Tokyo money market for the first time in over six months.
Overnight rates nudged up above the 0.50 percent discount rate in recent days on heavy commercial bank demand for funds and as talk stirred the BOJ might be thinking of tightening.
Today's surprise action brought money rates down to 0.48 percent from 0.53 on Thursday and killed the talk dead.

Dealers felt the reaffirmation of low rates in Japan should help underpin the relatively high yielding local dollar particularly as the risks of another policy easing in Australia had declined dramatically in the last couple of weeks.

Indeed, signs of an emerging pick up in the economy had turned the futures market around 180 degrees and the 90-day bank bill contract for December was now actually pricing in a tightening of around 70 basis points from the present 6.0 percent official cash rate.

The steady rate outlook helped keep the dollar firm on its Canadian and New Zealand counterparts in the dollar bloc and on most European crosses. That in turn saw it close at 59.3 in trade weighted terms unchanged from Thursday and a week ago.
Secondary data on new motor vehicle registrations today maintained the upbeat tone, rising 2.9 percent in January for a 5.0 percent gain on the year.

A raft of figures were due next week including Q4 GDP, January retail sales, Q4 inventories and merchandise trade. The Reserve Bank board also held its monthly meeting Tuesday but for once dealers expected no speculation.--Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
